title: Prophetic oracles shine with the greatest divinity-light: clear, named, and fulfilled
pass_a_gloss: Clause sense for XLII: the greatest light of divinity falls especially on the Prophets' oracles and inspirations (already discussed), and that light both persuades a pious faithful mind and strongly serves to refute enemies of God's Word and to prove divinity even against the profane. As to matter: the sacred oracles do not treat things of none or slight moment; they treat what looks to God's glory and the whole human race's salvation. Unlike once entangled ambiguous pagan oracles, prophetic oracles are clear and plain — often naming persons and place, and fixing fulfillment time beforehand with precision. They are not fallacious or uncertain; most already stand proved by the event itself.
pass_b_english: Especially in the Prophets' oracles and inspirations the greatest light of divinity shines — of which we spoke already above — because it not only suffices to persuade a pious and faithful mind, but also avails much to refute the enemies of God's Word and to prove its divinity even against the profane. For if you regard the matter of the sacred oracles, they are not about things of no or slight moment, but about what looks to God's glory and the salvation of the whole human race. Nor are the prophetic oracles entangled and ambiguous, as the pagans' oracles once were, but so clear and plain that persons and place are often named in them, and the time of fulfillment is fixed beforehand with precision. Nor are they fallacious and uncertain: by the event itself most have already been proved.
source_text: XLII. Praecipue in vaticiniis et afflatibus Prophetarum divinitatis maxima lux affulget, de qua jam antea diximus, quoniam non tantum sufficit ad pium et fidelem animum persuadendum, sed etiam plurimum valet ad verbi Dei hostes redarguendos, et divinitatem illius comprobandam etiam adversus profanos. Nam si vaticiniorum sacrorum materiam spectes, non sunt de rebus nullius aut exigui momenti, sed quae ad Dei gloriam et totius Humani generis salutem spectant. Neque prophetarum praedictiones perplexae sunt et ambiguae, ut Ethnicorum olim oracula, sed clarae adeo, atque perspicuae, ut in iis personae et locus designentur propriis saepe nominibus, et precise complementi tempus praefiniatur. Neque etiam sunt fallaces et incertae, sed tales ut ipso eventu pleraeque jam comprobatae sint.
